2026-04-26.text:
Midday sun hit the volcanic spires hard as we moved through the west side of the park, tracing Chalone Creek before looping back along the cliffs.

**Highlights:**

- [Pinnacles National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnacles_National_Park) — formed from the remnants of an ancient volcano that migrated ~200 miles north along the San Andreas Fault; one of the smallest U.S. national parks yet a critical recovery site for the California condor
- [Balconies Cliffs Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnacles_National_Park#Hiking) — winds beneath dramatic rhyolite talus caves where boulders wedged between canyon walls create natural tunnels used by roosting Townsend's big-eared bats

2026-04-27.text:
Morning light on Live Oak Road before heading south along the coast to San Luis Obispo, where we spent the afternoon exploring the area near Cal Poly.

**Highlights:**

- [Paso Robles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paso_Robles,_California) — sits atop a geothermal aquifer that feeds natural hot springs, which drew settlers long before the wine industry took hold
- [San Luis Obispo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Luis_Obispo,_California) — home to the Madonna Inn, and famously ranked among the happiest cities in the U.S. by multiple well-being indices
- [California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Polytechnic_State_University,_San_Luis_Obispo) — its "learn by doing" motto is backed by a working on-campus farm and ranch spanning over 9,800 acres

2026-04-28.text:
Morning light at Morro Bay State Park gave way to an afternoon walk along the coastal bluffs above Los Osos, the estuary glinting below under clear skies.

**Highlights:**

- [Morro Bay State Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morro_Bay_State_Park) — home to one of the few remaining great blue heron rookeries in California, with nesting birds visible from the park's museum grounds
- [Bluff Trail, Montana de Oro / Los Osos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_de_Oro_State_Park) — the trail edges Morro Bay Estuary, a nationally significant estuary supporting over 250 bird species and critical eelgrass habitat
- [Baywood–Los Osos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baywood-Los_Osos,_California) — an unincorporated community bordering the estuary, notable for resisting incorporation efforts and maintaining a distinctly rural coastal character

2026-04-29.text:
Early morning light at Pismo Beach gave way to a midday stop near Avila Beach before returning to the Pismo shore for the afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [Pismo Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pismo_Beach) — once famous for its Pismo clam harvest, which collapsed so severely that commercial clamming was banned; the beach also sits atop a monarch butterfly overwintering grove visited by tens of thousands annually.
- [Avila Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avila_Beach,_California) — the town was largely demolished and rebuilt in 1998–2001 after an underground Unocal oil spill contaminated the entire downtown area.
- [Dinosaur Caves Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur_Caves_Park) — named for a now-demolished roadside attraction featuring a large concrete dinosaur that once marked a tourist cave complex beneath the bluff.

2026-04-30.text:
Cool coastal air and a quiet pier marked the morning before a stop at one of California's smallest towns in the afternoon.

**Highlights:**

- [Cayucos, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cayucos,_California) — a small Central Coast beach town whose 1875 pier is one of the oldest surviving wooden piers in California, originally built by Captain James Cass to offload cattle and dairy goods
- [Harmony, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony,_California) — an unincorporated community with a permanent population of roughly 18, the entire 1875 Old Creamery complex was sold as a single property in 1994 and now houses artists' studios and a winery

2026-05-01.text:
Morning fog still clung to the hillside as we moved between the guest cottages and main grounds of Hearst Castle, then dropped down to the coast to watch elephant seals on the beach below.

**Highlights:**

- [Casa del Sol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Castle) — one of three Spanish Colonial Revival guest houses on the Hearst Castle estate, designed by Julia Morgan and named for its sun-facing position on the hill
- [Casa del Monte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearst_Castle) — the smallest of the three guest cottages, featuring hand-painted antique tiles sourced from Spain and Portugal
- [Piedras Blancas Elephant Seal Rookery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piedras_Blancas_elephant_seal_rookery) — a year-round colony where males can weigh up to 5,000 lbs; the colony unexpectedly established itself here in 1990 after decades of absence from California

2026-05-02.text:
Fog still clung to the shore at midday before we drove inland to wine country for the evening.

**Highlights:**

- [Moonstone Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonstone_Beach,_Cambria) — a narrow boardwalk-backed strand named for the translucent moonstones historically found among its pebbles; sits at the western edge of Cambria where the Santa Lucia Range meets the Pacific
- [Paso Robles Wine Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paso_Robles_AVA) — one of California's most thermally extreme AVAs, with daily temperature swings of up to 50°F that stress vines into producing intensely concentrated fruit; CA-46 bisects the appellation east–west through its densest vineyard corridor

2026-05-03.text:
Cool coastal fog clung to the cliffs as we pulled over along CA-1 in Big Sur on a Sunday afternoon, both shots captured within the same minute.

**Highlights:**

- [Big Sur, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Sur) — a 90-mile stretch of coastline so rugged it wasn't fully connected by road until 1937; the region has no incorporated towns and remains one of the least developed coastlines in the contiguous U.S.
- [California State Route 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_State_Route_1) — the segment through Big Sur required decades of convict labor and Depression-era CCC work to carve into near-vertical Santa Lucia Range cliffs.
